page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The c9g.8xlarge achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and static web serving throughput. Geekbench testing places both single-core and multi-core metrics in the top tier, alongside software compilation with clang and text processing. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and cached memory bandwidth read-only small block rank in the top 25 percent. Large block uncached memory operations and medium-model LLM inference speeds fall within the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture delivers high compute density per core, making it efficient for parallelized workloads. However, tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core, which limits its applicability for memory-intensive databases. The arm64 architecture also lacks x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX. The instance is suited for CPU-bound tasks such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and multi-threaded decompression workloads.
